# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 92 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 92 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_092_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 9

**1** "Now the stones that came from the plain and were fitted into the building of the tower in the place of those that were rejected — who are they?" I asked. **2** "These," he said, "are the roots of the white mountain. Since those from the white mountain were all found innocent, the lord of the tower commanded that these from the roots of this mountain be brought, in order that the tower might be completed. **3** For he knew that if these stones were to be placed in the building, they would remain shining and none of them would grow dark, as those brought from the other mountains have. **4** But since the tower had to be finished, and on account of these the lord commanded them to be brought immediately, and placed in the building." **5** "But what is the plain, and the other mountains?" I asked. **6** "All these mountains and the plain," he said, "are one world. **7** For this reason the lord called all these peoples to come and bring stones to build the tower, so that the tower might be completed. **8** And this is why the white stones from the plain are the same as those from the white mountain — for all share the same nature. The difference is that those from the plain came from the world directly." **9** "But why then were so many stones cast out and found not to fit?" I asked. "How many were cast out altogether?" **10** "The first round ones," he said, "are the worldly wealthy who, when affliction comes and hear of it, deny their Lord." **11** "And who are the rough ones?" **12** "These are those who have known the truth and have not remained in it, but fell away from the saints, and the recklessness and unbelief of their spirit made them rough; they were cast out."

---

*EMET: the plain = the world; the white mountain = the community of pure believers. The round stones = worldly wealthy who cannot fit the square tower due to unresolved worldliness.*
